title: The UK Commercial-Premises Compliance Economy
decision: Determine whether a defensible business should generate demand, manage compliance workflows, partner with accredited providers, acquire an operator, or remain out of the category.
verdict: Test a narrow partner-led managed-compliance operation, beginning with fire-risk and asbestos workflows, while keeping AI inside evidence-linked assistance and bounded agents. Reject generic compliance content as the core asset, defer pure SaaS until the operational wedge is proven, and defer acquisition until confidential diligence.
methods: Current primary-source review of UK and devolved fire-safety guidance, HSE guidance, energy-performance rules and official enforcement statistics
Obligation-by-obligation separation of required outcome, dutyholder, purchase trigger, competence boundary and review cadence
Reuse of retained read-only Google Ads historical metrics and selected Companies House filing evidence from the linked rank-and-rent publication
Purposive live-web comparison of horizontal property-workflow software, maintenance platforms and UK fire-assessor software
Actor-workflow-mechanism AI-disruption analysis across current, 2028 and 2030 horizons
Transparent conservative, base and upside scenarios rather than a market-size forecast
Adversarial test of self-provision, incumbent bundling, agent bypass, customer capture of savings, data non-accumulation and operating liability
Release-threshold design for jurisdiction, extraction, evidence provenance, credential resolution, action drafting, anomaly detection and false closure

normalization.aiDisruptionScore: Each AI dimension is scored from 0 to 5. For substitution risk, generated-content supply, discovery disruption, agent bypass and platform dependency, 5 means greater exposure. For operating leverage, proprietary data, physical moat, trust and liability, relationship moat and defensibility, 5 means greater advantage. Scores are displayed separately and are not summed into one net AI score.
normalization.entryStrategyScore: Seven dimensions use 0 to 5 scores. Weighted score equals demand necessity 20%, AI durability 20%, credible trust path 15%, proprietary-data potential 15%, recurring-revenue potential 15%, time to evidence 10% and capital efficiency 5%. The score informs but does not determine the verdict; unknown liability or competence can veto a high score.

exclusions: No Supabase query, production-system mutation, outreach, provider contact, professional advice, live acquisition action or paid-demand test
No claim that every commercial premises must buy every listed assessment or certificate
No extrapolation from rateable properties to a serviceable market without property, asset, dutyholder and purchase-trigger evidence
No claim that Companies House records prove current trading quality, margin, coverage or partnership intent
No claim that a model-generated report, image, checklist, recommendation or signature is inspection evidence or professional certification
No confidential customer reports, building-security information, personal data or raw private exports
limitations: This is a commercial research paper and not legal, fire-safety, asbestos, gas, electrical, water-safety, engineering or energy-performance advice.
Fire law and guidance differ across England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland; several non-fire HSE sources apply to Great Britain rather than every UK jurisdiction.
The official property stock uses rateable hereditaments rather than unique buildings, businesses or buyers.
Official fire audits are risk targeted and cannot estimate the compliance rate of all premises.
Public price pages are indicative supplier or marketplace statements rather than transaction microdata, achieved margin or national tariffs.
AI capability sources include vendor-authored claims. They establish product direction, not reliability, adoption, safety or achieved customer savings.
No authorised historical report corpus, shadow deployment, buyer interview, provider interview, contract, willingness-to-pay test or acquisition diligence was available.
Human evidence seams are retained as unknowns rather than represented as completed work.
observedFactBoundary: Observed rows restate what an opened source or retained dataset supports. Derived rows show their formula or claim inputs. Inference rows identify supporting claims and uncertainty. Unknown rows remain unresolved.
